items.title: 52043_Herman Autrey oral history interview
items.q: Well the feeling -- yeah, yes, yes I did. I felt it.

ctx.x: Now, I don't care who you are, you'd have to -- oh it'd be done better than I sang it, of course, but I mean, with that -- surrounded with those things happening, it makes you think and hear that type of voice, it have to mean something to a person. I don't care where they're from. They could be European, they could be -- well, what's happening? What's that? You just say well (snap) that sounds (snap) -- that sounds right (Snap) (Hums), bah wo dee (snap) dee (snap, bee (snap) bah-m-dee(snap) dee (snap) dee…
Right. You -- before, you mentioned one other trumpet player who you feel had an influence on you. Tommy Ladnier.
